newsitem.title: USA: Paper companies report earnings down.
newsitem.headline: Paper companies report earnings down.

text.p: International Paper and Consolidated Papers Inc. Tuesday reported sharp drops in quarterly profits as high industrywide inventories kept paper prices low.

Purchase, N.Y.-based International Paper said its first quarter earnings dropped 65 percent to $34 million, or 11 cents a share, from $98 million, or 36 cents a share. Sales rose to $4.9 billion from $4.8 billion.

"Although demand was generally strong, industry inventories remained high throughout the quarter. As a result, prices continued to decline, adversely affecting our earnings," said International Paper Chairman John Dillon.
Dillon said he believed the company was "finally at the bottom of a difficult business cycle" and expected the second quarter to be stronger.
The producer of printing papers, packaging and forest products said it has balanced production with demand and raised prices recently for uncoated grades of paper due to rising demand.
Meanwhile, Consolidated Papers Inc. said its profits dropped sharply in the first quarter, primarily due to depressed selling prices for the company's coated printing papers.
The company's first quarter earnings fell to $28.1 million, or 63 cents a share, from $52.7 million, or $1.18 a share, primarily due to depressed selling prices for coated printing papers.
The Wisconsin Rapids, Wis.-based company also said the decline in its profits, which began in late 1995, may have bottomed out.
The company said demand for some of its printing papers and coated speciality papers for magazines and catalogues was stronger during the first quarter.
